findings.detail: ITEM 1, CONFIRMED. The LEVERS READ line read `mode, dropout`; an AST walk over every `tok.<attr>` in the body returns exactly ['dropout'] -- the body's only read is `drop = float(tok.dropout) if regularize else 0.0`. THE LINE WAS THE WRONG HALF, not the body, and the reason is this package's own one-declaration rule: what tokenize emits is a function of the Vocabulary IT IS HANDED plus that one lever, and mode's effect is already frozen into that vocabulary by build_vocabulary (mode='bytes' returns a table with no merges, so _segment's match loop `range(hi, 1, -1)` finds nothing to take; mode='fixed' closes `ceiling`). Making the body read `mode` instead would let a 'bytes' Config handed to an 'online' vocabulary make the mode win over the table that is actually there -- a second declaration of a decision another entry point already made. Line now reads `LEVERS READ: dropout`, and the explanatory paragraph was placed ABOVE the block, never under it, because under it the parser's block terminator (tests/test_contract.py::stub_reads) would swallow the prose INTO the lever list -- the exact hazard build_vocabulary's own docstring documents. NO K4 CREDIT MOVED: TOK's harvested lever set from tests/test_contract.py::stub_reads is byte-identical before and after (19 names, `mode` and `dropout` both still present); `mode` keeps its credit from build_vocabulary, which declares AND demonstrably reads it (`mode = str(tok.mode)`), and from on_window. build_vocabulary's paragraph quoting the old sibling line was updated in the same edit so the quote is not left stale.

AFTER: same command -> 'body reads: [dropout] / LEVERS READ raw: dropout'. findings.detail: ITEM 2, CONFIRMED, and the count of five is exact. Enumerated by AST in BOTH directions (declared = every `tok.<name>` in a DID IT FIRE block; written = every `*.counters["..."]` subscript and every Gate(name=...) construction). DECLARED BY THE TWO IMPLEMENTED ENTRY POINTS AND WRITTEN BY NO BODY ANYWHERE: tok.build_pass, tok.build_mint, tok.build_converged (build_vocabulary) and tok.dropout_skip, tok.byte_fallback (tokenize). Written and matched already: tok.segment, tok.retok, tok.retok_noop, tok.load_reconciled, Gate tok.build_passes_advice. REVERSE DIRECTION, two rows: tok.load_reconciled_detail is WRITTEN by _replay_merges and was declared nowhere; tok.v0 is declared and is written as the FIELD vocab.v0, not as a counters key. FIXED BY WRITING THE BODIES, never by deleting a declaration. The three build rows are seeded and incremented only on the fresh-build arm; tok.build_pass counts passes EXECUTED (incremented after the size>=target test) and tok.build_converged is set ONLY on the minted==0 break, because 'the corpus ran out of pairs' and 'the target was reached' are different outcomes and conflating them would print a false equation. The two tokenize rows are fed by a new keyword-only `counts` accumulator on the private _segment, passed ONLY from tokenize -- build_vocabulary's three counting segmentations pass nothing, so the two numbers an operator reads are the RUN STREAM's and not a sum over the build sample under a name that means one of them. ABSENT vs PRESENT-AND-0 IS OBSERVED THROUGHOUT, the convention _replay_merges already states for tok.load_reconciled: the build keys stay ABSENT on mode='bytes' and on the replay arm (the loop is unreachable there) and tok.dropout_skip stays ABSENT at the shipped TOK_DROPOUT=0.0, where the branch cannot be taken. tok.load_reconciled_detail is now declared; tok.v0's row now says where it lives and why it is not copied into counters (a second home for a number that already has one).

findings.detail: ITEM 3, CONFIRMED. The comment said `counters` is 'Empty here and populated by build_vocabulary at each of its return points, never appended to piecemeal'. BOTH WRITERS CONTRADICT IT. Writer 1, _replay_merges: `vocab.counters["tok.load_reconciled"] = len(lines)` is written from inside the replay, not at a return point, and build_vocabulary itself wrote no counters key at all before this round. Writer 2, tokenize: `vocab.counters["tok.segment"] = vocab.counters.get("tok.segment", 0) + 1` and the same read-modify-write for tok.retok and tok.retok_noop -- appended to piecemeal, once per call, for the life of the vocabulary. THE COMMENT WAS THE WRONG ONE OF THE THREE: both statements are true of `gates` (build_vocabulary ASSIGNS the whole tuple at each of its three return points) and had been carried across onto the field beside it. Rewritten to separate the two fields: gates whole-surface-per-call, counters cumulative-over-the-run and appended to on purpose (there is no return point at which a total could be assigned, because the total is the point of the row), plus the ABSENT vs PRESENT-AND-0 rule that item 2's counters now follow.
findings.repro: The two writers, by grep -n 'counters\[' src/tok/api.py: 494 and 496 in _replay_merges, 659/666/667 in tokenize (line numbers at the time of reading, cited by symbol above). Neighbour: `vocab.gates` is still a whole tuple assigned once per build on every arm -- [('tok.build_passes_advice', False, 2, 8, False)] on online, (..., None, 8, False) on bytes, (..., True, 2, 8, True) on fixed.

findings.detail: NOT ONE OF THE FIVE ITEMS -- found while reading tokenize() for item 1, reported separately so the ledger is not credited with an item nobody filed. THE NO-OP SKIP RETURNED A BPE-DROPOUT-DRAWN SEGMENTATION TO A CALLER THAT ASKED FOR THE DETERMINISTIC ONE. The guard was `if is_retok and drop <= 0.0 and cache[3] == stamp`: all three tests describe THIS call, none describes the cached ANSWER. The cache is written unconditionally, dropout arm included (by design -- so the next call has a real stamp), so a deterministic call landing on a regularized entry was handed that entry's Segmentation object back. That contradicts this function's own docstring ('used for the TRAINING stream and never for held-out text, generation, or the final segmentation, which must be deterministic') AND it was counted as tok.retok_noop -- a row whose entire meaning is 'the rebuild would have been byte-identical' -- so the ledger printed a FALSE EQUATION rather than nothing. FIX: the cache tuple grows a sixth field, whether that answer came from a draw, and the skip additionally requires `not cache[5]`. The entry stays usable as a STAMP and becomes unusable as an ANSWER, which is the distinction the five-field tuple could not express; the rebuild is then counted as tok.retok (real work), not tok.retok_noop. No signature moved -- _retok_cache is private, is read at exactly one site, and grep -rn '_retok_cache' src/ tests/ docs/ tools/ finds it only inside src/tok/api.py.
findings.repro: <scratch>/repro_cache.py TOK_MODE=online TOK_SEED_VOCAB=320 TOK_DROPOUT=0.3, one regularized call then one deterministic call on the SAME bytes object. BEFORE: 's_det IS s_reg: True', 'len(reg), len(det): 165 165', 'len(truth): 150' (truth = _segment at dropout=0.0), 'det == truth: False', counters {tok.segment: 1, tok.retok_noop: 1} -- 15 tokens of dropout noise, 10% of the segmentation, delivered as the final deterministic one under a counter saying nothing had changed. AFTER: 's_det IS s_reg: False', 'len(reg), len(det): 165 150', 'det == truth: True', counters {tok.segment: 2, tok.retok: 1}. NEIGHBOUR, the shipped default TOK_DROPOUT=0.0: identical before and after -- 's_det IS s_reg: True', 'det == truth: True', counters {tok.segment: 1, tok.retok_noop: 1}; the no-op skip still fires and no recorded result moves, because cache[5] is False on every entry there.
